title: Hierarchical KV fractional reclamation and kernel swap protocol
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: As sequence lengths and multi-tenant footprints grow, our paged KV backing store sees fine-grained fragmentation and oscillating hotness across segments. Full-page eviction is often too coarse: it forces expensive decode rework or kernel fallbacks that raise P95 latency. Goals: 1) reduce P95/P99 prefill latency regressions caused by aggressive eviction, 2) lower total decode token cost by improving reuse of partially-populated segments, 3) provide a kernel-swap protocol so serving runtime can transparently move between heavyweight decode kernels and lightweight fragment-reuse kernels without client-visible correctness regressions.
technical_summary: Introduce a hierarchical segment model (segment -> microstripe -> fragment) with fractional reclamation: reclaim microstripes first, compact fragments opportunistically, and only evict whole segments when occupancy below a hard threshold. Coordinate with kernel selector via a lightweight Kernel Swap Protocol (KSP): KSP publishes hint vectors (expected prefill horizon, fragment hit-rate) and allows the selector to switch to a fragment-friendly kernel variant or full-decode kernel. Add admission-controlled prefill backpressure that charges a reclaim budget per tenant to avoid thrash.
design_decisions: Represent KV residency at three granularities: segment (256KB), microstripe (16KB), fragment (2KB).
Fractional reclamation prefers microstripe draining with epoch-based soft locks to avoid decode stalls.
Kernel Swap Protocol uses per-request hint header and a shared runtime scoreboard; kernel swap must be idempotent and revertible on failure.
Admission control tied to a per-tenant reclaim credit; credits accrue when tenant traffic is low and are consumed during large prefill bursts.
We will implement compact-on-write for fragments during low-load windows instead of synchronous compaction on eviction paths.
tasks: Spec: KSP message shapes, scoreboard semantics, and failure modes (ENG-501234-spec)
Runtime: hierarchical residency data-structures and microstripe allocator (ENG-501234-allocator)
Kernel: implement fragment-friendly kernel variant with sparse KV reads (ENG-501234-kernel)
Backpressure: per-tenant reclaim-credit accounting and admission controller (ENG-501234-backpressure)
Testing: unit tests, loadbench scenarios, and regression harness against p95/p99 (ENG-501234-tests)
Observability: new metrics (fragment-hit-rate, microstripe-evict-rate, kernel-swap-count), and Console dashboard tile (ENG-501234-metrics)
Rollout: canary on staging -> dedicated pool -> progressive rollout to hosted API with automated rollback on p99 delta.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for allocator, KSP, and kernel variant merged into main
Under synthetic mixed-tenancy load (1000 tenants with Zipf(1.2) seq lengths) P95 prefill latency improves by >= 20% vs baseline
Observed token decode cost reduced by >= 12% on the benchmark suite where fragment reuses occur
Kernel swaps don't introduce correctness regressions: no served sequences with missing or corrupted KV entries in 48h soak
Metrics emitted and wired to Console; alerting when kernel-swap rate > 10x baseline for a tenant.
risks: Kernel swap edge-cases where partial fragment metadata mismatch could cause decode fallback and increased p99 unless careful validation added
Per-tenant reclaim-credit tuning may be tricky for bursty customers leading to unfair degradation
Compaction work scheduled during 'low-load windows' could collide with other background tasks and still increase  tail latency if not rate-limited
mitigations: Add a KSP validation phase: two-phase commit for kernel swap with fallback scoreboard state and a short grace period
Start with conservative reclaim-credit defaults and expose tenant-level knobs in Dedicated/Private before enabling in Hosted
Use rate-limited compaction worker with CPU/GPU budget caps and measured backoff to avoid interfering with hotpath serving
test_plan: Unit tests for microstripe allocator and fragment lifecycle
Integrations: end-to-end prefill/serve scenario with injected cold starts to ensure fragment reuse
Load: run k6 and internal loadbench with mixed-tenancy profiles; compare decode token counts and p95/p99 latencies
Soak: 72-hour canary in staging with kernel-swap instrumentation and integrity checks
rollout_plan: Canary: route 2% of traffic in staging -> monitor metrics 24h
Staged: roll to a dedicated GPU pool serving internal beta customers (1 week)
Hosted: progressive ramp 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers on p99 delta > 15% or CPU/GPU compaction > 30%
